title: Failed marking never traps a learner
statement: If automated marking fails, spend no try and give no verdict; after repeated failures, show the authored answer, let the learner move on, and label it unchecked, not earned.
example: The lesson walk forces every scoring call to fail and requires all 5 of its degrade assertions to pass.
detail: The grade-3 rulebook makes it a standing rule that a broken scorer must never trap a child: marking degrades open, to a keyword fallback or an unjudged full pay, always with honest wording such as 'Checked by you this time'. Where a gate lets a child past after repeated failures it must first show the authored reveal, a rule added after a bare 'Move on' exit left a child knowing less than the question asked. An unjudged moment pays in full because the system's failure is never charged to the child, while progress ticks show neutral, never earned, when nothing was scored. The lesson walk forces every scoring call to fail and asserts that the app answers honestly, never claims the answer was good, never opens the gate on the first failure and eventually offers a way past.
against: A live walk found the scoring service timing out after 28 s on 4 of about 30 calls: Next stayed locked for the 28 s and then opened, 'so the fallback works, but those exchanges were probably not scored' (grade3-reading/artifacts/qc-2026-09-30-staging/LIVE-WALK.md, lines 86-89).
